deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is a short list of proofreader's or editor's queries headed 'Bemerkungen' (Remarks). Each query refers to a page and line of a printed or typeset text on human anatomy that is not identified on the page. The entries read:

(1) p. 258, second paragraph from the top: the last citation, 'Henle Muskellehre', lacks a page number ('Seite ??').

(2) p. 268, line 13 from the bottom: a citation to the 'Knochenlehre' lacks a page number. This is presumably Henle's as well, since it follows the previous entry.

(3) p. 264, line 1 from the top: a query whether the name should be 'Transversus costo-cervicalis'. The continuation line is hard to read ('... sein?').

(4) p. 263, line 6 from the bottom: 'dieselbe Frage' (the same question).

(5) p. 265, line 6 from the top: 'is the page 238 correct?', i.e. a cross-reference check.

(6) p. 271, line 9 from the top: a query about the nerve name 'N. cutaneus externus', with 'externus' underlined, suggesting doubt about that term.

The references are to Jakob Henle's 'Handbuch der systematischen Anatomie des Menschen'. Its Knochenlehre volume appeared in 1855 and its Muskellehre volume around 1858. Henle was a Göttingen colleague of Riemann from 1852.

The queried text deals with neck and trunk muscles (pp. 258-271) and peripheral nerves. It could be a monograph or journal article by a Göttingen anatomist or physician, or Henle-school material, for which these are proof corrections. Riemann's only known physiological-acoustical work, 'Mechanik des Ohres', appeared posthumously in Henle and Pfeufer's 'Zeitschrift für rationelle Medicin'. However, it does not concern cervical muscles or cutaneous nerves, so this sheet is probably not related to it.

The page also cannot by itself establish that the hand is Riemann's.

No derivations exist to reconstruct.
